This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-storage`, touching **21** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-access-hooks.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

- `content/docs/api/environment-routing.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/... (route, a path literal in a comment in AttachmentRemovalRouteLedgerEntry))_
- `content/docs/api/plugin-endpoints.mdx`  _(via sys_attachment (literal, a string literal in object))_
- `content/docs/deployment/single-project-mode.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/... (route, a path literal in a comment in AttachmentRemovalRouteLedgerEntry))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-access-hooks.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7d4b9ee302e4036cad269021a6677e7e325835e5` — the merge of head `e5aa3112bdbf29d0cef2c5d8c28b8d6ad6758bd7` into base `6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7d4b9ee302e4036cad269021a6677e7e325835e5 && git checkout 7d4b9ee302e4036cad269021a6677e7e325835e5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3 e5aa3112bdbf29d0cef2c5d8c28b8d6ad6758bd7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3 && git merge --no-ff e5aa3112bdbf29d0cef2c5d8c28b8d6ad6758bd7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

review#2 (server area pilot) · area A3 · Fixes #33010 · declaration face (`Clause-②: yes (widening)`: one route added). Read at high effort as an authorization change.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Matches the ruling (6879388034).** A member removes only attachments they uploaded, and the member grant gains no delete bit: `storage_attachment_member` is untouched, and the dogfood CONTROL case pins `security/explain` as read ✓ create ✓ delete ✗ and the data door's `DELETE /data/sys_attachment/:id` still `403` for the uploader.
- **The door is the shared core one** (`registerOwnRowDeleteRoute`, `packages/core/src/security/own-row-delete-routes.ts`, already serving comment reactions and personal views). Every refusal comes before any removal: caller, then 401, then held sign-in, then query parameters refused, then the row read **as the caller**, then `uploaded_by === caller`. Only then is the row deleted by id under `isSystem` with `attributedUserId` = caller and the caller's `tenantId`. This PR supplies only `{ object: 'sys_attachment', ownerField: 'uploaded_by' }` and the mount.
- **The owner column cannot be forged by a caller.** The attachment `beforeInsert` stamps `uploaded_by` from the session over any client value and refuses a session with no user. The column is `readonly` on update. Only a system write can set it otherwise, and that is trusted by definition.
- **The read as the caller** runs the object grant, the organization wall and `installAttachmentReadVisibility` (a row is readable exactly when its parent is). So an attachment on a record the caller cannot see answers `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND`, the same as an unknown id, the uploader's own included. That is the data door's answer and leaks nothing (pinned in the integration test).
- **What the system delete skips:** only the one `beforeDelete` on `sys_attachment` (the attachment delete gate, whose uploader limb would admit this row anyway, `attachment-access-hooks.ts` ~660). `afterDelete` still runs, so the file is tombstoned when no other row holds it (pinned: "its file is tombstoned").
- **A non-uploader is `403`** (another member, a parent editor, an administrator), and the row stays. Removing someone else's attachment stays on the data door behind an explicit grant, as the ruling scopes it.
- **Route:** `DELETE /api/v1/attachments/:id` collides with no existing route on `main`. It has its own ledger row (`gap`: the Console panel moves to it in the console half, and `@objectstack/client` has no method yet), the conformance test, live-mount parity, and `check-route-envelope` coverage. A server without DELETE routes mounts nothing and warns.
- CI on this head: 59 success, 9 skipped, none failed. `mergeable_state: clean`.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/service-storage` patch with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` (a new route; no export moves; every existing answer unchanged) and `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. `Skills-docs` names `content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx`, which documents the door, its four refusals and its row in the enforcement table.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Authorization: no wider grant. The admit is structural (one row, one person), on the same core door two other objects already use.
- The ruling's ADR-0090 D5 sentence is in the companion PR #33407 (governed, separate), which is allowed by the ruling's "same PR or a docs PR beside it". The two should land together, or #33407 soon after.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
- Nit N1: the route lives outside the storage family's `basePath`. An app that mounts storage under a custom base still gets `/api/v1/attachments/:id`. That is consistent with the other fixed own-row doors and is documented in the ledger note.

Implemented-by: `claude/area-A3-33010`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4cxDxAYxdtDhtR1kQQe`

**VERDICT: PASS**

所以失败的测试可能在本 PR 没碰过的包里 —— 那不是重排能修的。每次盲目重排都会让排在后面的所有 PR 重建一轮。

**分类：`failure`** —— 按下面的日志分诊。

**失败的 job（日志抽取，best effort）：**

- **[Test Core (5/8)](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/43633136778/job/132564696659)** — 失败步骤: Run this shard's tests

  ```

    ↳ 失败原因: @objectstack/rest:test: Error: Test timed out in 5000ms.
  ```

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
> 断言的对象是**这次实验自身的有效性前提**（跑完的耗时、负载下的先后、任何只在时间预算内才成立的条件）⇒ 它跟**超时**是同一类，同样对负载敏感，重排一次是合法的判别手段。
> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；
> `AssertionError: this run took over a second, so second-precision stamps could have differed too: expected 1006 to be less than 1000` 测的是实验前提：它守护的那条不变式当时是绿的，同一个 head 原样重排一次即成功。
> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）
